title: Stability-Compensated Threshold Calibration for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.21384v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models often produce hallucinated answers, motivating selective prediction policies that abstain on uncertain queries. However, heuristic uncertainty thresholds alone do not provide statistical control of errors among accepted predictions. Linear Expectation Constraints (LEC) reduce selection-conditioned error rate (SCER) calibration to a nonpositive expected linear-loss constraint, but the associated loss is non-monotonic in the acceptance threshold. We construct an exact counterexample under i.i.d. sampling demonstrating that LEC's empirical threshold-selection rule can violate the population SCER target. To address this risk-transfer gap, we introduce Stability-Compensated Linear Expectation Control (SC-LEC), which uses the negative linear risk of a theoretical full-data reference to compensate for threshold-selection instability. translated_title: 大语言模型中选择条件化风险控制的稳定性补偿阈值校准

tldr: 该论文针对大语言模型选择性预测中LEC方法阈值校准可能违反选择条件化错误率目标的问题，提出了SC-LEC方法，利用理论全数据参考的负线性风险补偿阈值选择不稳定性，并提供有限样本保证。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SC-LEC, a stability-compensated linear expectation control method that addresses the risk-transfer gap in LEC-based threshold calibration for selection-conditioned error rate control in LLM selective prediction, supported by finite-sample certificates.
